name: authentik
tagline: An identity provider built for small teams to self-host
description: An identity provider with single sign-on over OpenID Connect and SAML, plus a login proxy and LDAP and RADIUS interfaces for software that supports neither. Sign-in, enrolment and recovery are assembled from configurable flows.
licenseNote: The core is MIT-licensed and covers single sign-on, multi-factor sign-in, the proxy and the LDAP and RADIUS interfaces. Some features, such as pushing accounts to Google Workspace or Microsoft Entra, belong to a paid Enterprise edition. Check the current split before relying on a feature.
backing: Authentik Security, Inc. (US), a venture-backed company funded by Enterprise subscriptions

maturity.rationale: Released steadily for years, well documented, and now backed by a funded company. Younger than Keycloak, and releases arrive fast enough that upgrades are worth testing first.

selfHosting.summary: The official Docker Compose file brings up the server, a worker and PostgreSQL in a few minutes. The work is in what follows: connecting each app, setting up outgoing mail for recovery, backing up the database, and deciding what happens when the login server itself is down.

strengths: Covers awkward software too: a login proxy for apps with no single sign-on, and LDAP and RADIUS for older systems
Can create and remove accounts in other apps over SCIM
A clear admin interface, with sign-in and enrolment flows you can change without writing code
weaknesses: Open core: some integrations need the paid Enterprise edition
A fast release pace means upgrades need attention

featureNotes.multi-tenant: Separate branding per domain rather than fully separate organisations
